title: CIA-UAP-014, British activity in the Field of "Unidentified Flying Objects"
what_is_it: A classified CIA memo for the record summarizing British government activity in investigating unidentified flying objects, based on a briefing from a British messenger.
interpretation_warnings: The source text is an OCR extraction from an image of a typewritten document, resulting in numerous character-recognition errors that may affect accuracy of specific names and terms.
The document is a secondhand report — the CIA officer is recording what a British messenger told him, making this a single-source account.
Moderate redaction is present, with some names and details obscured or illegible.

The reference to a 'perfect flying saucer' at the Yorkshire RAF field is ambiguous — it is unclear whether this describes an unidentified aerial object or a deliberate demonstration/test of some kind.
The name 'Guladss' for the French Academy author is likely an OCR error and may refer to a different historical figure.
A more redacted version was previously public; this release under Section 1842 of the NDAA contains additional previously classified content.

verifiable_claims.claim: The British had a standing committee on flying saucers that had been operating for approximately sixteen months by December 1952.
verifiable_claims.source_quote: The British have had a standing committee created about sixteen months ago on Flying saucers

verifiable_claims.claim: The committee concluded that UFO observations were not considered dangerous and none had been seen over Britain.
verifiable_claims.source_quote: the observations are not considered dangerous and that none have been seen over Britain

verifiable_claims.claim: A 'perfect flying saucer' was observed at a Yorkshire RAF field during a demonstration attended by high-ranking RAF officials from London.
verifiable_claims.source_quote: In some RAF field, where some sort of demonstration to which high officials of the RAF in London had been invited. During the show, a 'perfect flying saucer' was seen

verifiable_claims.claim: The Yorkshire incident prompted press articles and was considered disturbing because it affected public opinion, which was part of Jones's responsibilities.
verifiable_claims.source_quote: articles appeared in the public press. This is disturbing to Jones because British control of the correction of public opinion is a part of his responsibilities

verifiable_claims.claim: A film from the Tremonton incident taken by a Naval non-commissioned officer was discussed, and Jones may request a copy.
verifiable_claims.source_quote: the film which had been taken by the Naval non-commissioned officer (Tremonton incident). It is possible that Jones will write asking for a copy of the film
